title: New license request: iPXE-UBDL-exception [SPDX-Online-Tools]
body:
**1.** License Name: UNMODIFIED BINARY DISTRIBUTION LICENCE
**2.** Short identifier: iPXE-UBDL-exception
**3.** License Author or steward: Michael Brown
**4.** Comments: This is proposal for a GPL license exception, that waives conditions of the GPL, when the distributed binary is built from already publicly available GPL licensed source. 

The license exception has been applied to the iPXE project source since 2015, and thus present in all major Linux distributions 

These two points satisfy the inclusion principles stated for the license exception list.

The upstream project has called this "UNMODIFIED BINARY DISTRIBUTION LICENCE" and describes licensing of source files as a choice between "GPLv2+ or UBDL", using their own custom license markup:

  "FILE_LICENCE ( GPL2_OR_LATER_OR_UBDL );"

IOW, upstream is treating it as if it were a standalone license. 

The actual text of the license, however, is waiving the need to comply with conditions of the GPL, and thus looks more appropriate as a GPL license exception, than a standalone license.
**5.** License Request Url: http://tools.spdx.org/app/license_requests/255
**6.** URL(s): https://github.com/ipxe/ipxe/blob/master/COPYING.UBDL
**7.** OSI Status: Not Submitted
**8.** Example Projects: https://ipxe.org/

Not Submitted

Author: Florian Roth (@Neo23x0); Steward: Nicholas Moore (nicholas.moore@grafana.com)

title: Autoconf-exception-generic: additional sentence
body:
This exception was found in RPM at https://src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/redhat-rpm-config/blob/rawhide/f/config.guess

`# As a special exception to the GNU General Public License, if you
  # distribute this file as part of a program that contains a
  # configuration script generated by Autoconf, you may include it under
  # the same distribution terms that you use for the rest of that
  # program.  This Exception is an additional permission under section 7
  # of the GNU General Public License, version 3 ("GPLv3").`

It is identical to `Autoconf-exception-generic` except in that it adds the final sentence about GPLv3 section 7.

For more info, see https://gitlab.com/fedora/legal/fedora-license-data/-/issues/220

What are people's thoughts on whether this last sentence makes it a different/new exception or if we could make that sentence optional in `Autoconf-exception-generic`

title: New license request: UnixCrypt
body:
### Introduction

Simple, permissive and historical license, apparently used in early Unix crypt utility.

Terms are very close to the [ISC license](https://spdx.org/licenses/ISC.html), with the following changes:
* "for non-commercial or commercial purposes" instead of "for any purpose"
* "without fee" instead of "with or without fee"
* requires retention of "this copyright notice" rather than "the above copyright notice and this permission notice"
* does not contain the second paragraph with the all-caps disclaimer language

Is open source, historical, believe it to be widely used given the reference to the Unix crypt utility. Is also used in at least one current Python library (passlib, see below) and in projects such as JBoss and Jetty.

### License Name

UnixCrypt License

### Suggested short identifier

UnixCrypt

### URL to license text

http://web.archive.org/web/20020702043523/http://www.dynamic.net.au/christos/crypt/UnixCrypt2.txt

### OSI Status

I don't know

Unknown

title: New exception: Autoconf macro exception
body:
<https://github.com/freedesktop/xorg-macros/blob/39f07f7db58ebbf3dcb64a2bf9098ed5cf3d1223/xorg-macros.m4.in#L1260>, also found in <https://www.x.org/releases/individual/app/xgamma-1.0.7.tar.xz>, uses an exception from GPL-3.0-or-later:

~~~~
As a special exception, the respective Autoconf Macro's copyright owner
gives unlimited permission to copy, distribute and modify the configure
scripts that are the output of Autoconf when processing the Macro. You
need not follow the terms of the GNU General Public License when using
or distributing such scripts, even though portions of the text of the
Macro appear in them. The GNU General Public License (GPL) does govern
all other use of the material that constitutes the Autoconf Macro.

This special exception to the GPL applies to versions of the Autoconf
Macro released by the Autoconf Archive. When you make and distribute a
modified version of the Autoconf Macro, you may extend this special
exception to the GPL to apply to your modified version as well.
~~~~

This exception looks distinct from <https://spdx.org/licenses/Autoconf-exception-2.0.html>.

It has already been approved for Fedora <https://gitlab.com/fedora/legal/fedora-license-data/-/issues/161>.

I need to add this exception to SPDX exception list and to determine an identifier. I propose "Autoconf macro exception" name.
